#### **<u>Highlights</u>** 

###### **China abolishes import VAT on gold contained in copper blister** 

China State Council approved to abolish the import value added tax on gold contained in copper blister, effective since November 1, 2009. China is highly dependant on copper resources import about 70%. Thus China Customs abolished the gold VAT of copper concentrate import since May 12, 2003 to support copper industry. However, affected by the financial crisis, copper producers were trapped again by the plummeting price. Raw materials were in short supply. Hence the gold VAT contained in copper blister was suggested to be canceled in early 2009. 

This policy is no doubt good news for domestic copper producers. 

1. It is helpful for copper producers to enlarge the purchasing channels of raw materials. In the first half of 2009, copper scraps supply declined sharply, which affected the refined copper production. As a result, enterprises had to purchase at high price to meet the need of production. Import of copper blister will ease the tight supply of raw material.

### **Macro Economy** 

**China's industrial output** is expected to grow by about 16 percent year on year this month and in December and the full year industrial output growth could reach around 10.5 percent, Minister of Industry and Information Technology Li Yizhong said on Nov.14. 

**China's consumer price index (CPI)** , a main gauge of inflation, dipped 0.5 percent year on year in October, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said on Nov.11. The rate of decline was 0.3 percentage points lower than that in September. 

**The producer price index (PPI)** , a major measure of inflation at the wholesale level, dropped 5.8 percent in October from a year earlier, according to the NBS. The rate of decline was 1.2 percentage points lower than that in September. 

###### **Copper price keeps on rising** 

Copper for three month delivery on the LME opened at US$6,318/t on Nov.2, closed at US$6,855/t on Nov.27, hitting US$7,055/t on Nov.26 and that on the SHFE opened at 50,430yuan/t, closed at 53,520yuan/t, touching a high of 55,500yuan/t on Nov.26. 

Affected by the performance of US dollar, US economy and climbing up inventory, copper prices fluctuated in early Nov. In the rest days, with capital flowing into the market, increasing open interest and strikes in several regions, copper price found support, in late Nov., it setting a year-to-date high of US$7,055/t. 

By Nov.27, the inventory on the LME warehouses was 435,075t, up by more than 60% since this mid-July, the volume of cancelled warrants was less than 2,000t, which indicated the demand (excluding China) was still gloomy. While in China the SHFE monitored inventory was staying high at more than 100kt since Nov. The big inventory on LME and SHFE restricted the rebounding of copper price. 

The miners in Spence Mine has not ended since they started in Oct. This month, a strike over wages by workers at Zambia's Konkola Copper Mines (KCM), a unit of London-listed Vedanta Resources, started. Workers in other copper mines are likely to strike. The news on strikes are supportive to copper price. If some strikes will continue, copper price is easy to stand above US$7,000/t. 

Although the fundamentals are still weak at the moment, people are worried about the over-performance of copper price, copper price is tending to climb up further. Investors are optimistic
